chapter: Mamie Smith and the New York dance bands
title: Summer at Asbury Park and Bobby Brown in Newark
summary: He and Walter Johnson commuted to Newark and worked with saxophonist Bobby Brown, who left music for a restaurant.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Well, let's just watch what, with Mamie Smith (unintelligible) 1924 -- oh, did summer season at Asbury Park, who was that with?
Oh, that was with -- Walter Johnson and I went with Robert -- Bobby Brown, a fellow from Newark, New Jersey, saxophone player.
Oh, Bobby -- what did he play, alto?
Alto sax, clarinet, named Bobby Brown.
And what happened to Bobby Brown?

Oh, Bobby, after we came back from New York, we were living in New York -- Walter and I used to commute over to Newark because they recall called it at that time Newark had quite a few places and a lot of musicians go like Kenneth Roane had a nice group over there. And Bobby Brown had a nice group over there.
So I stayed after the band. Bobby went into some business with his wife in a restaurant, and we came back to New York.
Oh, did he get out of music?
Yeah, he got out of music. Bobby --
